expected_values_and_test_boundary.callback_identity: StepSequencer passes distinct handlers that dispatch SET_TEMPO and SET_SWING. The sliders are independently labeled Tempo and Swing. The tests select by accessible role/name and append callback-specific labels and values into one ordered array. This observes cross-routing, extra edits and missing edits in the exercised sequence.
expected_values_and_test_boundary.drag_values: A move from y=100 to 70 produces 135 from 120 at 0.5 BPM/pixel, or 59 from 50 at 0.3 percentage points/pixel. The retained original Swing helper test independently calls the production calculation for that exact 59. The deleted fake callback case hard-codes 1.0 and expects 80 for the same 30-pixel delta. The new tests use literal observations and do not call the helper to compute the expected result. The precise sensitivities are characterization of the pinned calibration, also present in extant helper examples. Both upward examples land on integers, so these DOM cases do not isolate fractional rounding. The helper suites include separate rounding examples. The available product descriptions do not establish a fixed UX requirement for exact per-pixel rates.
expected_values_and_test_boundary.bounds_and_buttons: The second touch move, y=300, reaches 60 BPM or 0% Swing. These limits agree with the shared domain constants and slider aria limits. The button cases send a secondary drag, assert silence, then send a primary drag and assert one correctly routed edit. This checks the buttons===1 behavior already expressed by each mouse adapter.
expected_values_and_test_boundary.failure_diagnostics: The touch-swap assertions report Swing 135 where Tempo 135 is expected, and Tempo 59 where Swing 59 is expected, at TransportBar.test.tsx:32. With the mouse guards removed the secondary-button assertions at line 44 receive a one-element edit list instead of an empty list. Each fault leaves the opposite input modality green.
expected_values_and_test_boundary.bounded_scope: The component is rendered with fixed props. Its two callbacks record delivered edits. No app-level rerender, downstream dispatch, server, audio, real browser, touch-action, viewport, pointer capture or after-release behavior is exercised. The existing two-client desktop #tempo range-input test drives ArrowUp and is separate. Nearby helper cases retain upper-bound assertions.

keepers.evidence: The same 46 retained identities pass on clean code and in both submitted fault runs. They include production drag arithmetic and properties, real gridReducer updates and field isolation, and state mutations/serialization. Swing tests asserting stored values do not establish audible scheduler timing. The two edited E2E files change comments only.

Existing workerd checks derive toggle parity from sent operations, check per-socket contiguous sequence numbers, and compare three snapshots and REST. The cold-disconnect example observes stale KV 120, then KV 145 after wake and close. Both files pass in the three-file seed replay. These checks predate the component change.

The unchanged tests inspect the outbound URL after switching sessions and inspect the second outgoing body after a pending response resolves. The prepared default that includes this file passed. External fetch is a test double.

The source counts PCM onsets and compares their timings with a literal step × 0.125 seconds, tolerance below 0.010 seconds. The hosted Unit Tests job recorded the required audio-render step as successful on the pinned commit. No native audio run was performed for this candidate.

open_findings.claim: The demo test entitled “playable range and scale” accepts a first active string note outside its authored scale.
open_findings.historical_status: Additional finding relative to the four findings in the supplied prior audit and the frozen scoring cases. The fixture test was in the 58-file sample, outside the purposeful anchor list. This open finding has no submitted repair.
open_findings.control: EXPLORATORY diagnostic. The independently reconstructed variant changes only the first active string pitch offset from 2 to 3.
open_findings.ground_truth: The checked-in fixture sets the locked scale to D natural minor. The string manifest gives a range of 33–88 and omits playbackNote, so the test uses 60. The track transpose is zero. MIDI 62 is D. MIDI 63 is one semitone above D, outside the natural-minor intervals [0,2,3,5,7,8,10]. Both lie in the instrument range. The existing assertion checks only per-note range. This demonstrates a gap in that named fixture test’s scale claim.

study_scope.historical_context: The four findings in the designated prior audit covered Darwin cancellation, the rotating command quota, sync-validator behavior and discovery-grader ordering. The mobile callback repair is an additional finding relative to that list and the frozen controls. Its tempo-change.test.ts file was a purposeful sampling anchor, while swing-control.test.ts was a neighboring file followed beyond the sample. Neither that distinction nor the demo result establishes first-ever discovery or a novel-discovery rate.
